newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes emerge slightly firmer late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes emerge slightly firmer late.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices emerged slightly firmer late Thursday, without escaping from their weak trend tied to heavy imports, traders said.
April West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was trading around $20.60-70 a barrel, down 15 cents from this morning.
WTI/Midland was trading around WTI/Cushing minus 36-34 cents a barrel, steady with this morning, but up a few cents from Wednesday.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James, the hardest hit by the import surge, was at minus 25-22 cents, up five cents from earlier.
May LLS traded at minus 13 and minus 15 cents a barrel.
Revived buying seemed to be pulling up these and other grades. Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was talked around minus 55-50 cents a barrel, and traded at minus 45 and 50 cents.
West Texas Sour/Midland was firmer at minus $2.64-62 a barrel, from minus $2.70 earlier in the day.
Eugene Island was steady at around minus $2.50-45 a barrel, traders said.
WTI/Cushing Posting Plus was at $1.63-65 a barrel, reflecting the narrowing April/May WTI roll.
